anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Execution-plan costing is driven by stale, incomplete, or misleading statistics, causing systematic cardinality misestimation.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Engine runtime settings (memory, parallelism, checkpointing, etc.) are mis-tuned for the hardware and workload, creating artificial bottlenecks or under-utilization.
Storage I/O Throughput Anomaly : The underlying storage subsystem cannot supply the required read/write throughput or latency, producing sustained I/O waits and queue buildup.

When all three root causes are present, the database exhibits a multilayer performance collapse. Queries choose sub-optimal plans because of bad statistics, often opting for low-concurrency serial scans or over-parallelized plans that flood the already over-stressed I/O subsystem. Misconfigured memory, checkpoint, or work-mem parameters amplify the issue: insufficient cache increases physical reads, oversized work areas spill to disk, aggressive checkpointing surges write traffic, and mis-set parallelism spawns excessive workers that contend for limited I/O bandwidth. Observable symptoms therefore include extreme divergence between estimated and actual row counts, erratic plan flips after data loads, prolonged I/O wait times with idle CPU, surging checkpoint or log-flush waits, sudden throughput cliff after parameter changes, and highly variable query latencies that are hard to attribute to any single layer.

Causally, stale or poor statistics mislead the optimizer into selecting plans that either underutilize available memory (causing redundant random lookups) or overcommit it (forcing spills), both scenarios multiplying physical I/O. Simultaneously, sub-optimal configuration parameters—such as a too-small buffer pool or too-aggressive checkpoint intervals—reduce the engine’s ability to cache data and smooth write bursts, pushing even more traffic to disks. The compounded load meets an already bandwidth-constrained storage layer, where throughput saturation lengthens I/O service times. Rising latencies feed back into the optimizer’s adaptive components and background workers, triggering further plan recompilations, bloated execution queues, and longer recovery or maintenance cycles. Thus, each anomaly reinforces the others, producing a self-perpetuating degradation loop that impacts both transactional and analytical workloads.

entry.official_description: LOAD BULK DATA: Buffer pool size is %zu. Reducing concurrency from %zu to %zu. table=%s.
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with insufficient memory headroom, buffer pressure, oversized intermediate state, or memory-allocation constraints inside the engine or client library.
entry.solution_guidance: Check memory availability, per-session memory settings, large sorts or hashes, and whether workload concurrency is amplifying memory consumption.
